statement: The set of positive semidefinite symmetric matrices is convex: if M and N are positive semidefinite, then for any α between 0 and 1, αM + (1-α)N is also positive semidefinite.

steps.text: For any vector x, write the quadratic form of the convex combination as x^{\mathsf{T}}\left(\alpha M+\left(1-\alpha\right)N\right)x
Expand the quadratic form by distributing the vector multiplications to obtain \alpha x^{\mathsf{T}}Mx + (1-\alpha)x^{\mathsf{T}}Nx

Since M and N are positive semidefinite, we have x^{\mathsf{T}}Mx \geq 0 and x^{\mathsf{T}}Nx \geq 0. Since 0 \leq \alpha \leq 1, both coefficients are non-negative, which guarantees that the sum \alpha x^{\mathsf{T}}Mx + (1-\alpha)x^{\mathsf{T}}Nx \geq 0

assumptions.assumption: M and N are symmetric positive semidefinite matrices of the same dimension, and alpha is a real scalar in the interval [0, 1]
assumptions.breaks_when: The dimensions of M and N do not match, or alpha lies outside the range [0, 1].
